subject: ventures/3d-print-price-calculator
professional: someone who runs a small 3D print farm and quotes print jobs commercially (Etsy/Shopify plus custom orders); first they check that the machine-hour cost (power plus depreciation) and the failure allowance are computed the way they would, that the marketplace fee default matches what Etsy actually takes (percentage plus fixed per-order fees), that a full plate of parts can be priced per part, and that the G-code import reads the file their own slicer (most often Bambu Studio) writes

evidence.correctness: Recomputed independently in Python (not using the author's tests) from the standard conventions (filament $ = g/1000 x $/kg, as PrusaSlicer's own filament-cost estimate does; electricity = h x W/1000 x $/kWh; straight-line machine depreciation = cost/lifetime hours x h; expected attempts = 1/(1-p) for a geometric number of trials), then compared with node calc.mjs: defaults give material 0.99, electricity 0.0576, depreciation 0.25, buffer 0.1128, total 5.4938, break-even 6.0041, price 9.7235, all equal to the tool's output. The failed-print guide's table (5% vs 25%: buffer 0.07/0.43, total 5.45/5.81, break-even 5.96/6.35, price 9.64/10.29, +$0.64, $18 on 50 parts) matches to the cent. Cura length-to-grams: 10 m of 1.75 mm at 1.24 g/cm3 = pi x 0.875^2 x 10000 / 1000 x 1.24 = 29.83 g; tool 29.82 to 29.83. G-code parsing was checked against fixtures built from the line formats in the BambuStudio and OrcaSlicer source (GCodeProcessor.cpp), not the author's fixtures: PrusaSlicer, Orca (non-Bambu printer) and Cura headers parse right (29.46 g, 1.98 h); a Bambu Studio file fails to give a time (see completeness). The arithmetic is right. Kept at 3, not 4, because the default 8.5% fee is below Etsy's 6.5% transaction + 3% processing (9.5%) + $0.25 + $0.20 listing: at the tool's $9.72, the true Etsy margin is 29.4%, not the 35% shown.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features walked: cost breakdown and fee-solved price (works), break-even (works), check-a-price panel (works, tested), save/forget/share link (share.test.mjs, page.test.mjs), opt-out usage counting (usage.test.mjs), the three guide pages (served; https://marisstella.app/3d-print-price-calculator/ 200), and G-code import for five slicers. The import works for PrusaSlicer, Cura, Simplify3D and OrcaSlicer with a non-Bambu printer, but not for Bambu Studio, nor OrcaSlicer when the printer profile is a Bambu one: both write the time as '; model printing time: 1h 52m 3s; total estimated time: 1h 58m 40s' on one line (BambuStudio GCodeProcessor.cpp:715, Orca :1316), and gcode.mjs:53 only matches a line that starts with 'total estimated time'. Result on a Bambu-format header: ok=false, missing=['print time'], so the page asks the user to type the time. It fails loudly, not with a wrong number. No TODOs or stubs found.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/3d-print-price-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 77 pass, 0 fail, 0.19 s. quality_mutate.py, 6 core mutants: 5 caught (failure multiplier 1/(1-p) -> 1+p; electricity x1.25; labor and packaging inflated by the failure multiplier; actual profit off by packaging; Bambu-time regex branch removed). 1 survived: dropping otherFixedCost from totalCost (calc.mjs:121), because every test uses the default 0. The deeper gap is that the Bambu fixture in gcode.test.mjs:22 is a made-up line ('; total estimated time: 1h 30m 0s' on its own), not the format Bambu Studio writes, so the test passes a feature that fails on real files.
evidence.craft: Files read: calc.mjs (163 lines, pure, validated inputs with field-named errors), gcode.mjs (90 lines, regex parsing, no I/O, tested), share.mjs (derives its field list from DEFAULTS rather than copying it), index.html script (reads only the head and tail 256 KB of large G-code files, sensible). Clean and small. Defects: Number('') is 0, so a blank grams or wattage field silently prices as 0 (calc.mjs:26; node: blank grams and wattage -> material 0, electricity 0, price $7.71, no warning); the .gcode.3mf that Bambu Studio exports by default is not accepted (index.html:22, accept list), which is acceptable but undocumented.
evidence.claims: Checked: the fee-solving formula and the 1/(1-p) claim (backed by calc.mjs and recomputed); 'post-processing and packaging are not inflated' (calc.mjs:120-121, mutant caught); the guide's worked numbers (recomputed, pass); 'never uploaded' (gcode.mjs has no I/O, tested; FileReader slices only); the disclaimer (index.html:103 and all three guides, plus not-affiliated wording on the slicer page). Not backed: index.html:23 and README.md:43 say import reads 'Bambu Studio' files; it does not read their print time. README.md:55-56 says 'nothing is saved when you close the tab, every field resets on refresh by design', contradicted by the Save button and shared link the page itself describes (index.html:87). llms.txt lists github.io URLs in source, but the served llms.txt is rewritten to marisstella.app (checked), so not a defect.
evidence.fitness: Job: price one part for an Etsy listing. A hobby seller can do it in a minute and gets an honest breakdown and a fee-solved price. A print-farm operator hits three things in the first hour: (1) no parts-per-plate field, and the G-code import fills in the whole plate's grams and hours, so a 10-part plate imported as is gets priced as one part; (2) the Etsy fixed fees ($0.25 processing, $0.20 listing) have no field of their own (the note at index.html:69 says to fold the listing fee into 'other cost'), and the 8.5% default is below Etsy's 9.5%; (3) a Bambu user must type the time by hand.
evidence.domain: Compared with common print-farm costing practice (machine-hour rate = power + depreciation + maintenance; failure allowance; per-plate costing divided by parts per plate) and Etsy's Fees & Payments Policy (6.5% transaction fee on item price plus shipping, 3% + $0.25 US payment processing, $0.20 listing; etsy.com/legal/fees returns 403 through the proxy, so these are the published figures as of the auditor's knowledge). Matches: the cost lines, depreciation by machine hours, the fee folded into the price denominator. Departs: (a) the failure model charges every failed attempt a full print's material and hours; most failures (first-layer adhesion) stop early, so 1/(1-p) is an upper bound, and the guide's own example (a failure 'at hour six of eight') isn't parameterised; (b) no maintenance or consumables (nozzles, build plates) beyond the purchase price; (c) no batch/plate quantity; (d) the default fee understates Etsy's and the fixed fees aren't modelled. Each is within the stated limits, but a farm operator would not sign off the defaults as is.

defects.what: G-code import cannot read the print time from Bambu Studio files (or OrcaSlicer files for Bambu printers): those slicers write '; model printing time: X; total estimated time: Y' on one line (BambuStudio GCodeProcessor.cpp:715, Orca :1316), and the regex only matches a line that starts with 'total estimated time'. The import fails with 'Could not find print time'.
The page and README say the import reads Bambu Studio files; it does not read their print time.
The Bambu fixture is a made-up line ('; total estimated time: 1h 30m 0s' on its own), not the format Bambu Studio writes, so the test passes a feature that fails on real files.

The 8.5% default 'marketplace + payment fee' is below Etsy's 6.5% transaction + 3% processing = 9.5%, and the fixed $0.25 processing and $0.20 listing fees have no field of their own. At the default suggested price ($9.72), the real Etsy margin is 29.4%, not the 35% shown; the Etsy-correct price is $10.71.
No parts-per-plate quantity. The G-code import writes the whole plate's grams and hours into single-part fields, so an imported multi-part plate is priced as one part unless the user divides by hand.

The failure model charges every failed attempt a full print's material and hours; most failures stop early, so 1/(1-p) is an upper bound, and the page doesn't say so or offer a 'share of print completed at failure' input.
README privacy line says nothing is saved and every field resets on refresh by design, contradicted by the Save button (localStorage) and shared link the page describes.
otherFixedCost is not pinned by any test: dropping it from totalCost leaves all 77 tests green, because every test uses the default 0.
A blank field is Number('') = 0, so clearing grams or wattage silently prices that line at $0 instead of raising an error (blank grams and wattage -> $7.71, no warning).

verdict: The pricing arithmetic is right: an independent recompute of the defaults and of the failed-print guide's 5%-vs-25% table matches to the cent, and the Cura length-to-grams conversion is right. 77 tests pass and 5 of 6 seeded mutants were caught. It misses the bar on claims. The page says G-code import works for Bambu Studio, but Bambu Studio and Orca, for Bambu printers, write the print time on a '; model printing time: ...; total estimated time: ...' line (per their source), which gcode.mjs:53 doesn't match. Real Bambu files fail to import, while the test passes on a made-up fixture. A print-farm operator would also flag that the 8.5% default fee is below Etsy's 9.5% plus $0.45 fixed (real margin 29.4% at the default price, not 35%), that there's no parts-per-plate field, and that every failure is charged as a full print. The fixes are small: a one-regex change plus a fixture from real Bambu output, an Etsy-accurate default with a fixed-fee field, a quantity field, and a corrected README privacy line.
